scope.coverageDescription: Actual final-render sheet02,03,05 for cost and price math;08–15 for b13-03 through final b24-03. Three selected final-frame samples per shot. This is sampled image inspection, not a complete moving-film or listening review.
scope.contactOrderCaution: Sheet columns are alphabetically early,late,middle; read the labels. They are not a playback sequence and cannot establish exact transition feel.

observations.observation: Selected math states show20.000đ selling price with12.000đ input and5.000đ fixed-per-loaf allocation, caveat not net profit. Following actual final frames show the short statement3.000đ chưa phải lãi ròng. Numbers are inside frame, no obvious cutoff. The baguet­te-breaking background is actual bread but does not establish any price.

b05 selected old-price state20.000đ has14.500đ input +5.000đ fixed and500đ remaining; late state22.000đ shows2.500đ remaining and−500đ change. b06 shows3.000→2.500 with customer+2.000 and input+2.500. This matches the illustrative model and distinguishes selling-price increase from retained amount. Real flour/oven visuals remain context.

Actual final middle/late states show20.000→22.000→22.440 with+10% then+2%, and phraseTăng chậm hơn. Giá vẫn cao hơn. The numerical level rises even as the growth rate falls. Illustration and same-quantity caveats visible; units not clipped.

Receipt terminal, produce-market card transaction and grocery bagging appear at the discussion of costs, possible surplus and customer choices. These are recognizable actions, not blank cards. People/location are generic stock and must not be called Hạnh or her real customers. Foreign market context does not demonstrate the fictional bakery total cost.

Receipt checking, dough handling, flour shaping and actual Vietnamese baguette filling lead into a calculator/documents shot and buyer-side question. Hands and principal objects visible; no black portrait bars observed in this sample set. Distant receipt writing is not the script’s illustrative financial statement.

Chapter4 heading asks about wage versus bread buying; backgrounds are flour shaping and dough lifting. They anchor bread production but do not show wage, payslip or household earnings, so narration carries the wage premise until the next graphic.

Selected final graphic states show500→477 ổ and approximately−4,5% with caveat that nobody buys only bread and one item does not represent household purchasing power/CPI. Actual hands tear bread behind the right-side graphic. Early/middle state contains500 before477 is introduced; not a missing final number.

More-money/fewer-bread conclusion runs over kneading/oven footage; broader household-spending caveat moves to grocery item selection and checkout handling. Bread/hand subjects stay visible after portrait-to-landscape cropping, although some views are very close. No portrait black side pillars in these selected final pixels.

Different shopper baskets and transactions support the point that household spending experiences differ. Chapter5 and price/cost/purchasing-power synthesis appear over real dough action; source shoppers remain illustrative, not data proving a local inflation claim.

Concluding questions use repeated dough kneading and baguette oven sets. Main hands/dough remain visible, no slide cards or cartoon cast in these selected frames. Visual variety is limited despite nonoverlapping source intervals.

CTA asks about breakfast price; moves from hand kneading and gloved shaping into actual Vietnamese baguette sandwich filling/wrapping. Late sample has hand leaving prep board after wrapping, not a frozen empty ending. No full-time subtitles or cartoon visible; short question label appears on first CTA shot.

issues.observation: Several consecutive/recurrent units alternate only a few recognizable kneading/oven sets. Different nonoverlapping intervals do not by themselves yield creative or semantic variety.
issues.action: Retain this limitation for user feedback and future shot selection; do not label the style professional/approved from frame count or source diversity.

issues.observation: Wage-increase passage is contextual bread making rather than visible wage/payslip comparison. The mathematical purchasing-power explanation only becomes visible inb18.
issues.action: Do not claim every clause has direct visible evidence; future correction can add actual contextual payroll/personal-budget action if it improves this passage.

issues.observation: No actual continuous listening or playback performed for this final-film inspection; short fades, spoken emphasis, music feel and perceived pace remain unverified by this report.
